sentences.text: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rahul Bharti, Judge
This is a September 2019 filed writ petition.

02. The cause of action which has led the petitioner to approach this Court with the present petition is his grievance as to the action on the part of the respondent no. 3 - the Collector Land Acquisition (ACR), Reasi whereby the petitioner's brother, who is respondent no. 4 herein, has come to be paid an amount of 28,92,888/- as 80% of the compensation with respect to acquisition of land of their father, namely, Chuha falling under khasra no. 97/98/99 in village Kundarorian tehsil Katra, district Reasi which was purported to be acquired by reference to land acquisition exercise initiated under section 4 notification dated 29.09.2010 for the purpose of construction of new Bus Stand in Katra.

03. At the time of filing of the writ petition in 2019, the petitioner is on record to say that no acquisition award has been passed and still 80% of the compensation for the acquisition of land of his father, namely, Chuha came to be released in favour of the respondent no. 4 to the exclusion of the petitioner without any reason known to the petitioner.
04.

The petitioner has referred to the fact that way back in the year 2010 he had made an application to the Collector Land Acquisition (ACR), Reasi seeking reference under section 31 of the Land Acquisition Act.

Said application of the petitioner has remained un-dealt and un-responded all along Shankar Dass vs State Of J&K And Ors on 16 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56995319/

sentences.text: 05. The petitioner has referred to the fact that the petitioner's father - Chuha and uncle - Kirpu were two real brothers who were joint holders of land measuring 13.1 kanals 11 sarsai in khasra no. 97/98/99 in village Kundarorian tehsil Katra, district Reasi.
The petitioner's uncle - Kirpu had no male issue and it is alleged that the respondent no. 4 was adopted by him so as to become his successor (Kirpu's successor).
06. In so far as the petitioner's father is concerned, he was survived by the petitioner, the respondent no. 4 and another son Teju.
Teju, the brother of the petitioner and the respondent no. 4 is said to have expired issueless and, as such, out of reckoning of succession to the estate of Chuha.

07. By this reference, the petitioner is meaning to say that it is he who alone is the inheritor of the estate of Chuha to the extent of his share in the aforementioned land and by that reckoning it is the petitioner alone who ought to have been paid the compensation but instead it is the respondent no.
4 who has been paid the entire compensation leaving the petitioner, despite being son of Chuha and successor-in-interest to his estate, unpaid with no amount of compensation paid to him for the reasons which are not known to the petitioner but only to the the Collector Land Acquisition (ACR),
Reasi.
08.

In this backdrop of the case, the present petition is lying awaiting the response on behalf of official respondents whose appearance came to be caused as is borne out in terms of an order dated 09.10.2019 as this Court had restricted the issuance of notice only for the respondents no. 1 to 3 considering the nature of the controversy involved.
09. Till date, the respondents no. 1 to 3 have not bothered to come up with any reply/objections to the writ petition and the writ petition is held up in a status quo.

In terms of an order dated 05.04.2023, the Hon'ble Division Bench, then seized of the present writ petition, had even put the official respondents on guard that in the event of non filing of the reply the Court would proceed in the matter on merits without response of the respondents and still it has not bothered the official respondents to submit their response in the case.
10.

Thus, as per the record position of this writ petition, this Court is not even aware as to whether any final land acquisition award came to be passed pursuant to section 4 notification no.
DC/RSI/09/2041-51/SQ dated 14.11.2009.

It is only from the final award that this Court can come to know about the fact as to with respect to land acquired in khasra no. 97/98/99 in village Kundarorian tehsil Katra, district Reasi who is land owner/s to whom the compensation has been held payable and paid and the amount of the compensation paid.

11. Under the circumstances, this Court is constrained to direct the the Collector Land Acquisition (ACR), Reasi to appear in person along with the production of final land acquisition award pertaining to the aforementioned section 4 notification.
